merger_description:
Waterfront Logistics HoldCo Pty Ltd (**Waterfront Logistics**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued shares in Monson Logistics Pty Ltd, Monson Shipping Pty Ltd and Monquip Pty Ltd (together, **Monson Logistics**) from Bruton Investments Pty Ltd, Bruce William Monson and Toni Anne Monson (the **Acquisition**).

Waterfront Logistics is owned by First Sentier Investors (Australia) RE Ltd as trustee of the Australia New Zealand Infrastructure Fund (trading as **Igneo Infrastructure Partners**). Igneo Infrastructure Partners is the infrastructure asset management business of the First Sentier Group, which is ultimately owned by Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group.

Waterfront Logistics, through its subsidiaries, operates the Strait Link business (**Strait Link**), which provides domestic shipping services across Bass Strait between the Port of Melbourne and the Port of Burnie, carrying containerised and roll-on/roll-off cargo. Strait Link also provides land logistics services in Tasmania and at the Port of Melbourne, including general and refrigerated freight, warehousing, rail operations and dangerous goods services.

Monson Logistics is a Tasmanian-based provider of freight transport and logistics services. Its services include road and rail transport, warehousing, Australian Border Force (**ABF**) and the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (**DAFF**) bond facilities, empty international container parks and Tasmanian Freight Equalisation Scheme (**TFES**) claims services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of landside
logistics services for general freight and warehousing in
Tasmania is expected to be low, and the increase in share of
supply arising from the Acquisition is expected to be small
b. the presence of alternative providers of landside logistics
services for general freight and warehousing in Tasmania
c. the Acquisition will not increase concentration in the supply
of bluewater shipping services across the Bass Straight
d. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition,
including due to the operation of the ABF/DAFF bond
facilities.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
